h1: The 8 Best Garden Auger Drill Bits Under $50 for Bulbs, Seedlings and Posts, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Garden Auger Under $50: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 garden auger drill bits under $50 for bulbs, seedlings and fence posts, compared on diameter, length and drill fit.
summary: The TCBWFY two-size set with a 1.6 inch and a 3.5 inch auger is the garden auger to buy if you plant both bulbs and larger seedlings, and the K-Brands 2 pack is the close alternative. The SYITCUN 4 by 16 inch is the pick for wide holes, and the MAXCCINO 2 inch is the mid-size compromise. Every one of these bits costs under $25.
intro: The usual mistake with a garden auger is buying for the hole and forgetting the drill. These bits only turn as well as the tool behind them, and a weak cordless drill with no clutch will stall in clay, twist your wrist and stop dead on the first buried root. Spend as much thought on the drill you own as on the bit, because the best auger in the world is a frustration on a 12 volt compact.

We reviewed eight listings, all of them auger bits that sit under $25, and ranked them by diameter range, length, shank fit and how well each suits the usual garden jobs of bulbs, bedding plants and small posts. The listings in this bracket give limited material detail, so we flag where a number is missing rather than guess. Price buckets replace exact prices throughout.

products.name: TCBWFY Garden Auger Drill Bit for Planting 1.6"x16.5"and 3.5"x16",Heavy Duty Bulb Planter Tool for Digging Holes,Compatible with 3/8" Hex Drive Drill
products.verdict: Two augers, 1.6 and 3.5 inches wide, covering bulbs through bedding plants for under $25.
products.description:
The TCBWFY set pairs a 1.6 by 16.5 inch auger with a 3.5 by 16 inch auger, both for a 3/8 inch hex drive drill. The listing calls it heavy duty and a bulb planter, and it fits any drill with a chuck that grips a 3/8 inch hex shank.

It takes first place because two diameters solve most of a gardener's tasks. The narrow bit is right for tulip and daffodil bulbs, garlic cloves and small seedlings, and the wide one makes holes for pots-worth plants, perennials and smaller shrubs. The tradeoff is that the 3.5 inch bit takes real torque, and a light drill will bog down.

Buy it if you plant a bit of everything and want one purchase to cover it. Skip it if you only plant tiny bulbs, where a single narrow bit is enough.
cons: Wide bit needs a stronger drill
products.idealFor: Gardeners planting bulbs and larger starts.

products.name: K-Brands Auger Drill Bit for Planting 2 Pack 1.6" x 16" & 3.5" x 16" Set
products.verdict: A matched 1.6 and 3.5 inch pair, both 16 inches long, under $25.
products.description:
The K-Brands set gives you a 1.6 by 16 inch auger and a 3.5 by 16 inch auger. The listing offers few other details, but the sizes are what matter: a narrow bit for bulbs and a wide one for bigger holes.

It lands second because the sizes closely match the TCBWFY pair, and the difference is a half inch of length on the narrow bit and a bit less listing detail. A 16 inch bit is plenty for planting bulbs at the usual depth, and it reaches well below the frost line in most gardens. The wide auger shares the torque demands of any bit that size.

Buy it if you want a well-sized pair from a brand that offers the same shapes in single-size listings too. Check the drill's chuck size before you order.
products.idealFor: Anyone who wants two sizes in one buy.
products.skipIf: You want a stated steel grade.

products.name: SYITCUN 4"X16" Heavy-Duty Auger Drill Bit for Planting - Garden Spiral Drill Bit - Bulb Planter Tool & Post Hole Digger - 3/8" Hex Drive
products.verdict: A 4 by 16 inch auger that doubles as a post hole digger for small jobs.
products.description:
The SYITCUN is a single 4 by 16 inch auger on a 3/8 inch hex shank, sold as a bulb planter and a post hole digger. A 4 inch diameter is wide enough for small shrubs, a mailbox-style stake or a lightweight fence post.

It ranks third because wide holes are the most demanding job for a hobby drill. Torque grows quickly with diameter, and a 4 inch bit will stall a weak drill or twist your wrist if it catches a root. Used with a corded or high-torque cordless drill at a low speed, it digs quickly in loose soil. In compacted clay or stony ground, expect to pull the bit out often to clear it.

Buy it if you plant mid-sized shrubs or set small posts and own a strong drill. Skip it for bulbs, where a narrower bit digs cleaner holes.
pros: Doubles as a light post digger
products.idealFor: Gardeners setting shrubs and light posts.
products.skipIf: You own a light 12 volt drill.

products.name: K-Brands Auger Drill Bit for Planting, 4 x 12 Inch, 3/8'' Hex Drive Drill
products.verdict: A shorter 4 by 12 inch auger that is easier to control than the 16 inch versions.
products.description:
This K-Brands auger measures 4 by 12 inches and uses a 3/8 inch hex shank. It is the same diameter as the SYITCUN but four inches shorter.

It ranks fourth because length affects control. A shorter bit sits closer to the chuck, flexes less and is easier to start in a straight line, which helps when you are drilling a shallow bed for annuals or herbs. The cost is depth: 12 inches limits you to modest planting jobs, and it will not reach the deeper holes some shrubs and trees want.

Buy it if you want a wide hole but never plant deep. Pick the longer SYITCUN if depth matters.
pros: Shorter bit is easier to control
Low cost for a wide auger
products.idealFor: Shallow planting of annuals and herbs.
products.skipIf: You need holes deeper than a foot.

products.name: MAXCCINO Auger Drill Bit for Planting 2"(D) x14.5(L), Garden Ground Earth Spiral Drill Bit for 3/8" Hex Drive Drill, for Post Hole Digger
products.verdict: A 2 inch by 14.5 inch auger sitting between bulb bits and wide planting augers.
products.description:
The MAXCCINO measures 2 inches in diameter and 14.5 inches in length, with a 3/8 inch hex drive. At 2 inches it sits just above the 1.6 inch bulb bits, which is useful for bigger bulbs, small perennials and seedling plugs.

It ranks fifth because it is a single mid-size bit with no companion, so you will still want another size for other jobs. It asks for less torque than a 4 inch bit, which makes it easier on a modest cordless drill. The listing also uses post hole digger wording, which is optimistic for a 2 inch bit, since that is only really suitable for thin stakes.

Buy it if your planting sits in the middle: bigger bulbs, young perennials and small plants. Skip it if you want a narrow bit for tiny bulbs.
pros: Lower torque needs than wide bits
cons: Too narrow for real post holes

products.name: TCBWFY Auger Drill Bit for Planting 1.6x16.5inch Extended Length Garden Auger Spiral Drill Bit for Planting Bulbs Flowers,Post Hole Digger
products.verdict: A single 1.6 by 16.5 inch bulb auger with extended length, for 3/8 inch hex drills.
products.description:
This TCBWFY bit is the single narrow auger from the same brand as the set. It measures 1.6 by 16.5 inches, uses a 3/8 inch hex shank, and the listing positions it for bulbs and flowers.

It ranks sixth because the set above gives you this bit plus a second size for only a little more. If you only plant bulbs, it is the right tool, since a 1.6 inch hole is wide enough for most bulbs and narrow enough to keep the soil in place. The extended length helps you reach planting depth in one pass without bending over.

Buy it if bulbs are the only job and you own a modest drill. If you plant anything bigger, step up to the two-size set.

products.name: SORANGEUN Auger Drill Bit for Planting - 1.6" x 16.5" Plant Auger for Cordless Drill - Bulb Planter Tool for Bulbs Planting&Holes Digging
products.verdict: A 1.6 by 16.5 inch plant auger written up for cordless drills and bulbs.
products.description:
The SORANGEUN measures 1.6 by 16.5 inches and is described as a plant auger for cordless drills. The listing gives few other details, so the shank, material and flute design are not confirmed beyond what the title says.

It ranks seventh because it matches the TCBWFY single bit in size but gives less proof of build quality. A narrow auger is a simple tool, and the differences between brands show up in thread depth, weld strength and finish, none of which the listing documents. A cordless drill with a 3/8 inch chuck is a good fit for this size.

Buy it if the price is lower than the TCBWFY on the day you shop. Otherwise, take the better-documented bit.
products.idealFor: Casual bulb planting with a cordless drill.

products.name: Garden Auger Drill Bit for Planting 1.6" x 16.5" -3/8" Hex Drive Compatible
products.verdict: An unbranded 1.6 by 16.5 inch auger with a 3/8 inch hex drive.
products.description:
This is a generic 1.6 by 16.5 inch garden auger that fits a 3/8 inch hex drive. The listing has no brand story and no material detail.

It ranks last because it offers the same dimensions as two ranked pieces above with less backing. Without a named maker, you cannot compare weld quality or finish, and returns are the only protection if the bit arrives bent or with a rough thread. At this price, that risk is small.

It makes sense as a throwaway bit for a one-off bulb planting project. If you plan to dig every season, a better-documented option is worth the few extra dollars.
products.skipIf: You plant every season and want durability.

whatMatters.detail: Diameter sets what you can plant. A 1.6 inch bit suits bulbs and garlic, a 2 inch bit handles larger bulbs and plugs, and a 3.5 or 4 inch bit makes holes for shrubs and small posts. Check the diameter in the title, because bigger bits demand much more torque.

A 12 inch bit is easy to control but shallow, while 16 inch bits reach full planting depth. Longer bits also flex more, so start slowly. Check the length in the listing, not just the box art, since some titles list the diameter only.
All eight here use a 3/8 inch hex shank, which fits most cordless drill chucks. Make sure your chuck opens that wide. A 12 volt compact drill will often stall on the 3.5 and 4 inch bits.

Garden soil hides roots and stones, and a bit that catches will spin the drill in your hands. Use a drill with a clutch or a low-speed setting, and hold the handle firmly. A side handle helps on wider bits.

A steel auger should resist bending, and a coated or painted one resists rust. Most listings in this bracket do not state a grade. Wipe the bit dry after use and store it indoors, since soil moisture rusts bare steel quickly.

faq.q: Will a garden auger fit my drill?
faq.a: All eight use a 3/8 inch hex shank, so any drill whose chuck opens to 3/8 inch can hold them. Most cordless drills do. Check your chuck size before you order, and avoid using an impact driver unless the maker says it is allowed.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with a garden auger?
faq.a: Running it too fast and pushing too hard. Use low speed, let the flutes carry soil up and out, and lift the bit now and then to clear it. Forcing a bit into a root can twist your wrist or stall the drill.

faq.q: Is the two-size set worth it over a single bit?
faq.a: For most gardeners, yes. A 1.6 inch and a 3.5 inch auger cover bulbs and bedding plants in one purchase at under $25. A single bit only makes sense if you plant just bulbs or just larger holes.

faq.q: Can I use these as post hole diggers?
faq.a: The 4 inch bits can set a light stake or a small fence post in soft soil, but they are not a substitute for a real post hole digger. Narrow bits are for planting only, and the post digger wording on listings is optimistic.

faq.q: How do I keep an auger from rusting?
faq.a: Knock off loose soil, wipe it dry and store it indoors, ideally with a light coat of oil. Soil moisture rusts bare steel quickly, and a rusty bit binds in the hole and digs more slowly.

faq.q: Do these work in hard clay?
faq.a: They can in moist clay, but dry clay and stones will stall a small drill. Water the spot the day before, use low speed, and pull the bit out often to clear packed soil. A stronger drill makes a big difference.

finalTake: For most gardeners, the TCBWFY set with 1.6 and 3.5 inch augers is the best garden auger under $50. The K-Brands 2 pack is a close alternative, the SYITCUN 4 by 16 inch is the pick for shrubs, and the single 1.6 inch TCBWFY covers bulb work for less. Pair the bit with a drill that has a clutch and low speed. A weak drill is the real limit, not the auger.
